text: The Killing form of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is the symmetric bilinear form defined by $B(X,Y) =$
explanation: The Killing form is $B(X,Y)=\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{ad}(X)\circ\mathrm{ad}(Y))$, the trace of the composite of adjoint operators. $XY-YX$ is the bracket itself, not a scalar-valued form; $\mathrm{tr}(XY)$ is the (different) trace form on matrices; and a product of two separate traces fails to be the Killing form.
